title: Mustard chicken with champ and greens

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a staple such as stock, wholegrain mustard and crème fraîche, with nothing from a jar or packet mix.

supermarket.reason: Potatoes, spring greens, spring onions, chicken breasts and the dairy are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only pans and a masher, and boiling, mashing, pan-frying and a quick pan sauce suit a confident beginner.

works.reason: 1kg potatoes, two bunches of spring onions and four breasts suit four people, the timings are sound, and mashing the greens into the champ still gives a good result.

honest_times.reason: Peeling the potatoes, shredding the greens and slicing the onions plus tending the chicken fits 25 minutes, and the 20 minutes of cooking run side by side believably.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and floury potatoes is a fair name for the potatoes id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Champ is built around the spring onions, which suits a still-chilly late March evening alongside spring greens.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Chicken, potatoes, greens and spring onions make a proper family dinner of real food.
